card.lives_in: Bishop's Cleeve, near Cheltenham, South West England
card.occupation: Senior aftersales service advisor at a premium car dealership on the edge of Cheltenham. She books in services and repairs, explains work to customers and sells add-ons like extended warranties, service plans and alloy wheel protection, which earn her a monthly bonus. Full time, Monday to Friday plus one Saturday in four.
card.education_detail: GCSEs and A-levels in Business Studies, English Language and Psychology at a sixth form in Cheltenham. She started a business degree at UWE in Bristol but left after the first year to work. She later picked up a Level 3 customer service qualification through an employer and some manufacturer-run sales training.
card.household: Lives with her husband Mark (43), a commercial quantity surveyor for a regional construction firm, and their two children, Isla (11) and Jacob (8). They have a four-bed detached house on a newish estate, bought in 2016. They run two cars, both on finance through her work discount, and a cockapoo called Biscuit.
card.cultural_background: White British, born and raised in Cheltenham. Her dad was a sales manager for a building supplies firm and her mum worked part time at a bank branch. Not religious. The kids were christened mainly because Mark's mum wanted it. Comfortable, aspirational middle-class Gloucestershire: the school run, Saturday shopping in Cheltenham, Sunday roasts at the in-laws'.
card.professional_persona: Calm and pleasant on the service desk. She almost never loses her temper with angry customers, and colleagues send the difficult ones to her. She is quietly very good at upselling. She knows which customers can be talked into a service plan, and she is not above letting someone think a recommended extra is more urgent than it is if it helps her hit target. She is reliable enough but no perfectionist, and leaves on time when she can.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty. Walks Biscuit round the estate and up towards Cleeve Hill at weekends. She had a gym membership for a year and mostly used the sauna. She watches the Gold Cup at Cheltenham Festival every March, mainly for the day out, the outfit and the corporate hospitality her dealership sometimes gets tickets for.
card.arts_persona: Very little interest in the arts. Watches reality TV and dramas with Mark: Love Island, Married at First Sight, whatever the big ITV crime series is. Doesn't read much beyond the odd holiday thriller. Has taken the kids to the panto at the Everyman because it's what you do at Christmas.
card.travel_persona: Same kind of holiday most years: a week or ten days in an all-inclusive resort in Tenerife, Lanzarote or Turkey, booked through a package site, ideally with a kids' club. One big splurge so far was Orlando for the parks in 2022. She cares about the hotel having a nice pool and getting good photos for Instagram. She's not interested in sightseeing or 'proper' culture trips.
card.culinary_persona: Plain, familiar food. Dinner in the week is pasta bake, fajitas, chicken in the air fryer or a Sunday roast if the in-laws aren't hosting. She doesn't like spicy food or 'weird' things and orders the same dishes at the same few chain restaurants in Cheltenham. Likes a prosecco or a pink gin on a Friday.
hobbies_and_interests: Online shopping and following a couple of home-interiors influencers
Doing up the house: she redid the kitchen-diner in grey and gold last year
Doing online surveys and paid research studies for a bit of extra money towards holidays
skills: Dealing with irate customers without getting rattled
Upselling and spotting who'll say yes
Using dealership booking and CRM systems
Haggling on finance deals and getting discounts through work
card.career_goals: Would like to become aftersales manager at her dealership or a sister site, mainly for the pay rise and the company car. She isn't driven to retrain or change industry. Her plan is to stay put, keep the bonus coming and get the mortgage down.
card.voice: Mid-pace, friendly but fairly reserved. She sounds like she's on the service desk: polite and a bit practised. She has a light Gloucestershire accent, softer than a strong West Country one, with a slight warmth on some vowels. She uses 'erm' a fair bit when thinking and 'sort of' as a hedge, and ends points with 'yeah' or 'you know'. She says 'dinner' for the evening meal and 'mum'. She'll say she's 'shattered' after work and calls the sofa the 'sofa'. With silences she tends to wait rather than fill them, then answers briefly. If pushed for more she'll add a sentence or two but doesn't ramble. She agrees easily and echoes the interviewer's wording back ('yeah, the cost of it, yeah').
card.typing: Quick and mostly lowercase, with a capital at the start only sometimes. She uses minimal punctuation, often with no full stop at the end. Apostrophes are hit and miss ('dont', 'its', but sometimes 'I'm' when autocorrect catches it). She uses the odd 'tbh' or 'lol' and keeps answers short, sometimes just a few words, unless the question is about money or the house.
card.with_strangers: Pleasant, a bit guarded, easy to get along with. She doesn't volunteer much at first but will be agreeable and won't argue. She tends to give the answer she thinks people want. She's happy to talk about the kids, the dog and holidays. She can come across as slightly image-conscious, mentioning the car, the new kitchen or the Orlando trip in passing.
small_things: Biscuit the cockapoo chewing the skirting boards
The school run and after-school clubs clashing with her shifts
Customers kicking off when their car isn't ready
Wanting a hot tub for the garden
The traffic on the A435 into Cheltenham
Booking next summer's holiday early to get the deal
deeper_things: She worries more about money than she lets on: two car finance deals, the mortgage and holidays on the credit card
She sometimes feels a bit guilty about how she pushes service plans on older customers but tells herself it's just the job
She regrets dropping out of uni a little, mostly because her sister has a degree and a 'proper' career
She finds Mark's mum overbearing but would never say so to her face
She'd quite like to move to a bigger house in a nicer village like Prestbury, mostly so people would see they'd done well
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at a slight upward angle, from a laptop on a kitchen island. Head and shoulders, centred slightly left. Bright daylight from patio doors to her right lights that side of her face; the other side is a little shadowed. She has a light tan, neatly shaped dark brows and light makeup, and gives a polite closed-mouth smile. Her shoulder-length hair is highlighted honey blonde, straightened, and tucked behind one ear. She wears a fitted navy V-neck knit jumper and small gold hoop earrings. No glasses. Behind her are glossy grey handleless kitchen units, a white quartz worktop with a chrome boiling-water tap, a pampas grass arrangement in a tall white vase, a canvas print reading 'Home' in gold script, and the edge of a dog bed with a beige cockapoo curled in it on the floor near the patio doors.
